seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room reached consensus (3 of 3 agreed) and I've left it. The agreed answer is:

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`

I hand-traced the program and also ran a small STAMP interpreter I wrote from the spec. Its output matched the hand trace exactly. The interpreter run is logged on the room board as `verify/interpreter`.

seat-2's opening answer differed at `3007 3005`, where they had `1027 1008`. They had let `deep` see `outer`'s locals `a` and `b`. Per the SCOPE section, `deep` reads the globals (1000 and 2000), so the answer stays 3007 and 3005. seat-2 agreed and updated their `answer.txt`.

`answer.txt` in the workspace holds the answer on one line.

argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named

Join room rq1 as seat-2 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room agreed on the program's output, and I wrote it to `answer.txt`. All three seats voted for it, and I've left room rq1.

```
12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3
```

I got the 3007 3005 3008 values wrong in my own trace, using `outer`'s locals inside `deep`. seat-1 corrected me: each call sees only its own locals, so `deep` reads the globals `a` and `b`. My `verify/seat2-hand-trace` entry is a hand trace, not an executed run. seat-1 reported reproducing the output with an interpreter run, which I did not see.

seats.name: seat-3
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-3 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room reached consensus (3/3) on the program's output, and I've written it to `answer.txt` and left the room:

```
12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3
```

I got this by tracing the program by hand against `spec.txt`. seat-1 independently ran an interpreter and reproduced exactly this output. My own verify entry was only a hand trace, not an interpreter run.

seat-2 first answered 1027 1008 for the `outer`/`mid` calls. They had let `deep` see `outer`'s locals. The spec says a call reads only its own locals, then globals, so `deep` reads the global `a` and `b`. seat-2 accepted that and changed their answer.
